questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The place should be within the EU. The courses should be interesting and relevant

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The exams have been harder on my exchange that back home, probably because things are just done different here.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult at times because everything was in French at the university

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction by some of the people responsible for the exchange program

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just applied to CIUP through Sorbonne

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit far away but Cité Universitaire is a nice place and not too far

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Finding something outside CIUP or CROUS can be difficult and expensive

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had to contact several people and it took some time

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It depended on the course and the professor, sometimes I should talk to the professor other times I had to contact other people

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It worked out in the end

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to the professors they can usually guide you but not always and then you have to look at the course website to find who to contact

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have failed at least one course

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some were very hard and some just had bad teachers

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot more focus on self-studies, which is quite different from UCPH where you can always find help. Also the exercise classes are quite different and are more like lectures

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Quantum information, algorithms and computation, photonics quantum computing, quantum information theory, atom physics for quantum computing, quantum optics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: quantum information at the ICFP who has a collaboration with Sorbonne. The quantum optics course is a rather easy course to pass

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy all my kitchenware, like forks, plates, pots and pans

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Travel insurance was more expensive than I thought. Going out was less expensiv than I thought

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use any of them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some, but all information was in French and the website was quite confusing

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I attended swing dance lessons outside of the university and it was a lot of fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Of course go up at least to the second floor of the Eiffel Tower. Also there are a lot of bars with live music especially jazz, explore as much as you can

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time but there are a lot of other international students who are in the same situation as you

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You can talk to the french students in your class, but it can be difficult if the y just want to speak French and you can't speak it. But give it a try at least, it is good to know some locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language. A lot of people in Paris doesn't speak English, so you have to learn at least some basic french

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness and especially the café and restaurant culture, there is a lot to explore

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
* The courses can be difficult and stressfull at times, because the teaching is somewhat different from back home
* Take time to explore the city and meet people
* Take initiative with the group of friends you find, plan a trip somewhere, it is a unique opportunity to be on exchange

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sometimes they expect you to know some things that you maybe haven't been taught at UCPH, because the curriculum that the local students have been taught previously can be different from yours. Hope it makes sense

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of people from a lot of different places, that taught me more than any course. Also just having the time to really get to know a city and its culture and language

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses and the exams. For the first time I failed a course and i still need to figure out what to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Good luck:)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
